reviewFindings: Mutation controls and the mutation handler enforce readOnly; forget preview and editor entry are guarded. Accepted/proposed/conflict pinned sources remain readable, including older conflict revisions. Existing writable callers default to readOnly=false.

The launcher requires current thread/project/working-copy ownership and the exact current-owner M05 read URL, readOnly=true, and a non-UNSUPPORTED module state. DISABLED and EMPTY retained reads are supported.
Memory owner-key remount and existing active/generation/AbortController checks remain intact. SourceWorkbench provider scope includes the App account/epoch and active/held fences.

The memory component runtime import remains behind explicit launch. The existing workbench shell, provider and composer subtree stay mounted. Proposal03 accurately asks for a window reload after import failure.

The two native Modal instances share existing primitives. Focus retention only rescues focus dropped to body and does not steal a deliberate move to the top dialog; cleanup restores the parent launcher. The browser cases verify both Escape returns.
The App header opener is restricted to pinnedThreadId&&!embeddedThreadId, removing the duplicate ordinary-main control while retaining the native pinned-thread control.

limits: Initial three memory failures all stopped at the missing Open memory review launcher; deeper readOnly and owner assertions were not reached in those failing runs.
Initial panel main case stopped at count 2 versus expected 1; native pinned case passed. No timeout or assertion was changed between red and green.
The queued memory/source case passed before and after this UI implementation. It is integration coverage, not a newly repaired defect.

The old in-flight source request was aborted with net::ERR_ABORTED. A separate newly opened wrong-account memory envelope was delivered and rejected by the actual client. Do not claim an uncancellable stale source response was delivered.
Memory/source HTTP and desktop bridge are typed scripted fixtures. These browser checks do not prove host authorization, real model dispatch, installed desktop, Windows or Edge behavior.
Only four selected workbench-app cases and two selected desktop-surfaces cases were run. Complete suites and other current gates remain owned by the parent.
